PLAN
- Phase 0 — Framing (1 day): Define swarm contract. All agents emit one artifact type: `candidate.json` (kind: signal|feature|hypothesis|regime_alert; payload; agent_id; timestamp; in-sample stats; provenance). Candidates never touch weights — they append to a new `candidates/` evidence store consumed by existing learning.py recompute path. Flag `SWARM_ENABLED=false` default.
- Phase 1 — Orchestrator (1–2 days): Simple Python overnight runner (reuses existing loop infra, not Slate) that invokes 6 Claude Code agents sequentially-per-stage, parallel where safe: IdeaGen+FeatureEng (parallel) → Backtester → Validator (maker) → RegimeAuditor+Decomposer (parallel) → Validator (checker pass). Persistent state = files in `swarm/state/` (agent memory, seen-idea dedup hashes) + existing evidence logs.
- Phase 2 — Agent specs (2–3 days):
  1. IdeaGen: reads weather/NWP papers (ingest queue), outputs hypotheses keyed to known biases (HRRR warm/cold bias by hour/regime, recency, formation time axes already in adaptive_tree).
  2. FeatureEng: transforms hypotheses into feature specs against existing hourly_engine joins; writes feature code to `swarm/features/` behind `SWARM_FEATURE_<name>` flags; never edits core features directly.
  3. Backtester: runs feature on settled OOS slices using existing backtest/daily_engine utilities; emits cal_err, edge, residual stats in same schema as evidence logs.
  4. Validator (maker-checker): maker = statistical pass (n_eff/events/days, multiple-testing correction via BH across the swarm's daily candidate batch, regime-stratified OOS); checker = independent re-run of backtest from raw data + schema/look-ahead audit (leakage linter on timestamps/formation times). Rejects write to `swarm/rejected/` with reasons.
  5. RegimeAuditor: labels synoptic/seasonal regimes (frontal passages, heat domes, seasonal month) from existing met obs; attaches regime tags to candidates and flags regime-conditional performance.
  6. Decomposer: runs factor/residual decomposition (reusing daily_engine residual_std/EMOS machinery) to confirm candidate adds orthogonal signal vs existing ensemble; kills correlated clones.
- Phase 3 — Gate handoff (1 day): Approved candidates become evidence entries consumed by learning.py: promotion still requires existing LEARNING→PROBATION→ARMED flow, cal_err+edge gates, independence, family borrow, drift demotion — unchanged. Swarm only accelerates candidate intake; stamping into adaptive_tree follows existing partial-stamping path.
- Phase 4 — Overnight ops (1 day): Cron/Task Scheduler nightly run; morning report (accepted/rejected counts, top candidates, BH-adjusted p-values); budget cap on agent tokens/night; DRY_RUN untouched; no execution-path changes anywhere in this plan.
- Phase 5 — Hardening (ongoing): maker-checker disagreement log; weekly human review of promoted candidates; swarm self-metrics (acceptance rate, post-promotion survival rate) feeding back to IdeaGen prompt tuning.

RISKS
- Look-ahead leakage in agent-generated features → mitigated by checker leakage linter + formation-time stamping.
- Multiple-testing inflation from high candidate volume → BH/FDR correction per batch; min n_eff enforced before validation.
- Short weather history → regime auditor requires per-regime n_eff; seasonal hypotheses need ≥2 seasons or family borrow.
- Agent overfitting to same biases (correlated ideas) → dedup hashes + Decomposer orthogonality kill.
- Framework creep (Slate) → deferred; Python orchestrator unless agent-count or parallelism demands it.
- Overnight run failures silently producing nothing → heartbeat log + morning alert on zero-output.
- Execution risk → none in scope; swarm output is research-only, never near maker execution paths.

CHECKPOINTS
- C1 (end Phase 1): Orchestrator runs 6 agents end-to-end on 1 toy hypothesis with SWARM_ENABLED=false.
- C2 (end Phase 2): 20 historical backfill candidates processed; leakage linter catches a planted look-ahead case; maker-checker disagreement <30%.
- C3 (end Phase 3): One swarm candidate completes full existing promotion path to ARMED with zero changes to gate code.
- C4 (after 4 weeks overnight runs): ≥10 candidates validated, ≥1 promoted, post-promotion cal_err within gate on live OOS.
- C5 (after 8 weeks): swarm-sourced signals show positive incremental edge vs baseline ensemble on settled OOS.

IF_FAIL
- C1 fails → reduce to 3-agent minimal (IdeaGen→Backtester→Validator) and retry.
- C2 fails (leakage linter misses plant) → halt swarm, harden linter, require timestamp/formation audit before any further runs.
- C3 fails (gate rejects everything) → expected/acceptable; tune Validator pre-screen thresholds upward, not the gate downward.
- C4 zero promotions → check candidate quality vs gate bars; add IdeaGen feedback loop using rejection reasons; do not relax gates.
- C5 no incremental edge → keep swarm running for idea intake but cap token budget 50%; reassess at 12 weeks; sunset if still flat.
- Any execution-path regression → SWARM_ENABLED=false (default anyway); swarm has no execution touchpoints by design.

DECISION_RULES
- Promote only via existing learning.py gates; swarm never overrides cal_err, edge, independence, or n_eff bars.
- Reject candidate if BH-adjusted p ≥ 0.05, per-regime n_eff below threshold, or Decomposer correlation >0.7 with live factors.
- Adopt Slate only if nightly runtime >4h or >2 agents need true parallelism that the Python loop can't provide.
- New feature code merges only with flag off + passing checker + human review; auto-merge never.
- Scale token budget only if prior week's promoted-candidate survival rate ≥60%; cut 50% if <30%.
- Any conflict between swarm recommendation and drift demotion → drift demotion wins.
- Seasonal/synoptic hypotheses require multi-season evidence or explicit family borrow; single-season OOS is insufficient by default.
